pull.title: validation: throw when a compressed script can't be decompressed
pull.body:
`ScriptCompression::Unser` ignores the `DecompressScript` return value and
leaves the script empty on failure, without notifying upper layers about the error.
In the worst-case scenario, which is currently only reachable through corruption,
an unspendable off-curve P2PK turns into an anyone-can-spend empty script.
Given that, properly throwing the error to prevent any future mistakes from
happening seems the sanest path to follow.

Aside from that, added coverage for a P2PK script with an uncompressed pubkey
that has a valid X but a wrong Y, which makes it unspendable. Checking we store
such scripts raw and never encode them as 0x04/0x05, as those encodings
serialize X with only Y's parity (not the full Y), which would make decompression
recompute Y from X and turn the unspendable script into a spendable one, which
would not be good.

test: script compression with off-curve and wrong-Y P2PK pubkeys

Adds coverage for two cases:

The existing compress_p2pk_scripts_not_on_curve test now also covers
the ScriptCompression ser + unser round-trip, and checks the behavior
of a compressed record that can't be decompressed.
The worst-case scenario is a P2PK to an off-curve pubkey, which nobody
can spend, that is turned into an anyone-can-spend script during
decompression without throwing an error to upper layers.
Note: this could only ever happen after corruption today, but better
to add proper coverage for it, and add the missing error signaling
(next commit).

Then added coverage for a P2PK script with an uncompressed pubkey that
has a valid X but a wrong Y, which makes it unspendable. Checking we store
such scripts raw and never encode them as 0x04/0x05, as those encodings
serialize X with only Y's parity (not the full Y), so decompress would
recompute Y from X and turn the unspendable script into a spendable one,
which would be bad.

events.body:
Concept ACK

Looks already pretty solid but I left a few, mostly minor comments.

> In the worst-case scenario, which is currently only reachable through corruption,

This does not sound like a valid use case for recoverable error handling to me. If this is a clear indication of corruption, it should be treated as such.

*Edit*: I see that all decoding errors are reported through exceptions, which is not great. But it means that the error handling in this PR is aligned. Hence, ACK.

Concept ACK, we have lots of similar findings that we should slowly plug, this seems like a good next step.

Could we also check how callers handle the new exception, especially where an unreadable coin could be silently skipped? Left a few suggestions for diagnostics and coverage too.

I’ll [follow up](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36386) separately on the `OP_RETURN` fallback potentially leaving a spendable script.

comments.body: Would you mind covering each type here already? It doesn't seem to be that complex and otherwise the test is weaker than it needs to be.
I guess this coverage wasn't that interesting but this is dropping the call of `DecompressScript` with different `nSize`.
Do we really need to check this 1000 times? If we do, then maybe this should rather be a fuzz test? For a unit test doing this once should suffice I think.

`nSize` is `type` (the compression format) and is still provided by the fuzzer and tested against the code. Diff is that we are providing it inside the data stream we feed to `ScriptCompression` instead of a direct func arg.

Happy to know if you are seeing something else.
Sorry, my comment wasn't that clear, what has changed is that the fuzzer doesn't cover `DecompressScript` with `nSize` >5 anymore, but as I said, not that important coverage I guess.

ah, last one checked against is 6 (`nSpecialScripts`), which check the raw script storage path (any number over 5 takes the same path). ~~This was on purpose because once we go over the last encoding format, we start consuming bytes from the script, which could make `nSize` to underflow and end up with a huge allocation.~~  <-- not true, I need caffeine.

nit: the script is the last field of a `Coin`, so nothing follows it in a chainstate value.
Undo records and snapshot files are where more data follows.
